thread:
Leila: Quick design question — how do we want gateway-driven fallbacks to honor client hints vs operator policies when capacity is tight?
Leila: Proposal A: accept X-RW-Model-Hint if signed by tenant (X-RW-Sig) and use it to prefer a specific variant in the fallback chain. Otherwise gateway picks best variant.
Sam: don't trust unsigned headers from clients. signed hints only. otherwise it becomes an attack vector (tenants could force expensive paths).
Matt: +1 to signed hints. Also prefer server-side tenant config over client hints when conflict. Client hint should be advisory, not authoritative.
Tasha: UX note — console should show "hint used" vs "policy override" per request so support can debug. Per-route chart with fallback_rate and hint_accept_rate.
Leila: Another thing — for cache reuse we should try to pick fallbacks that share tokenizer / arch so KV cache doesn't become useless. E.g., prefer quantized variant of same model family before switching to a different family.
Sam: agree. We can add a fallback metadata tag: model_arch + quant_tag and only allow reuse when matches. Otherwise we should mark cache miss.
Matt: Real concern: signed header requires key mgmt. We should let tenants sign a short-lived token (edge signs on behalf of tenant using tenant API key) rather than exposing private keys. That way we can validate at gateway without extra ops.
Leila: rough routing config idea (for RFC):
```yaml
routes:
  - match: "/v1/generate"
    priority: 100
    signed_hint_header: "X-RW-Model-Hint"
    fallback_chain:
      - variant: "modelA-v2-8bit"
        reason: "capacity"
      - variant: "modelA-v1-quant"
        reason: "cb_trip"
      - variant: "familyB-compact"
        reason: "last_resort"
    region_affinity: true
    telemetry_labels: ["fallback_reason","route_taken","model_variant"]
```
Sam: Also add header normalization step: strip X-Model-* from incoming unless X-RW-Sig passes validation. Log when we drop a header.
Tasha: For circuit-breaker we should emit events with cb_state transitions and capacity_pct. Dashboard: add a small table on route page showing recent cb_trips and the percent of requests that hit fallback because of CB.
Matt: Telemetry fields to add: fallback_reason (capacity|cb|quota|policy), original_hint (if any), hint_sig_valid (true|false), fallback_variant, previous_kv_key (for cache debugging).
Leila: Question on soft fallback TTL — if we swap to a fallback variant temporarily, do we keep KV entries tagged by original model for X minutes or flush? My instinct: keep entries but tag them with model_signature so fallback can attempt reuse if arch matches.
Sam: keep and tag. Flushing kills perf. But expose metrics for cache-mismatch-rate so we can tune fallback ordering.
Tasha: Console should surface a "fallback heatmap" for each tenant showing which routes fall back most, and a per-model panel showing average latency delta when fallback occurs.
Matt: Ops note — fallbacks must be region-local. Don't route to different region for fallback unless explicitly permitted by tenant; otherwise egress/latency/regulatory issues.
deploy-bot: deploy 1725001245: rolled canary of signed-hint validator to 10% of traffic in us-west-2
Sam: Nice — monitor hint_accept_rate and fallback_rate during canary. Alert if fallback_rate increases > 2x baseline.
Leila: I'll draft RFC with sample config + telemetry schema + console mocks and tag @Matt @Tasha for reviews. Planning to include migration and key rotation plan for the signing tokens.
Tasha: thanks — I'll mock the console widgets and add the fallback drilldown. :thumbsup:
Matt: ok, ping me when RFC is ready. I can add the telemetry ingestion schema and log enrichment.
Leila: will do. Closing loop here — thanks everyone!
